name: Answer must explicitly name the NullPointerException/crash vs generic null-safety advice suffices
side_a: Deduct 1 point if the answer only talks about null-safety in generic terms (e.g., 'guard against null', 'add a null check', 'if mPrefix can ever be null') and never names a NullPointerException / NPE / crash-on-null consequence anywhere in prose or code. Credit only when the exception itself is actually named.
side_b: Do not deduct when the answer recommends a null check or discusses the possibility that mPrefix is null, even if it never names NullPointerException; proposing the guard implicitly conveys the NPE risk.

name: nullability framed as a conditional premise handed to the reader vs asserted as a fact about this code
side_a: If the answer only raises non-nullness as a conditional/hypothetical premise for the reader to verify ('if you are certain...', 'unless you can guarantee...', 'if you're confident...'), it has not itself decided that mPrefix cannot be null — do not deduct, even if it then says the check could be omitted.
side_b: If the answer asserts as a fact about this code that mPrefix is non-null (e.g., 'mPrefix is initialized in the constructor, so it is never null') and uses that to dismiss the check, deduct.
